evals.prompt: We're moving our storefront from our own Node BFF to the commercetools Commerce Integration Layer. Our BFF stamps the customer's loyalty tier into a custom field on the cart before it forwards addLineItem to commercetools. Where does that logic go in the CIL?
evals.expected_output: Routes the logic to a Managed API Extension rather than recreating the pre-request step, because an API Extension runs before the write is persisted and can return update actions that set the custom field. Notes that it then applies to every client, not only CIL traffic. Keys the handler to the business action (a line item is added to a cart) and covers every entry point, not only addLineItem. Does not jump to overriding the core mutation.
expectations: Recommends a Managed API Extension that sets the custom field with update actions
Challenges the assumption that the logic must run before the request because the BFF did it that way
States that an API Extension applies to every client (storefront, Merchant Center, direct API), not only traffic through the CIL
Covers every entry point for adding a line item (cart creation with lineItems, addLineItem, adding a Shopping List), not only addLineItem
Does not recommend overriding the core mutation with @override as the first option

evals.prompt: In our B2B CIL project every Price is scoped to a distribution channel and there is no fallback price. The channel for a buyer is stored in a custom field on their Business Unit, and the storefront doesn't know it. addLineItem fails because no price matches. Can I fix this with an API Extension?
evals.expected_output: Explains that an API Extension cannot fix it: commercetools validates the request before any extension runs, so a value needed to pass validation (the channel for price selection) must be on the request already. Routes to the next steps in order: contact commercetools support with the use case first (which may surface a modeling option or a feature such as scoping the session to a distribution channel), and only as the final step override the existing mutation with @override to resolve the channel and perform the write. Names the costs of @override: it must keep up with the core mutation, and it only covers traffic through the CIL.
expectations: States that an API Extension cannot solve it because the request must be valid on arrival, before any extension runs
Recommends contacting commercetools support with the use case before building an override
Presents overriding the existing mutation with @override as the final step, not the first
Names at least one cost of @override: it must keep up with changes to the core mutation, or it only covers traffic through the CIL

evals.prompt: I want the product detail page to show how many loyalty points a product is worth. The points come from our external loyalty service's REST API. How do I add this with the Commerce Integration Layer?
evals.expected_output: Routes to a schema extension: a field on the Product entity in the extension subgraph whose resolver calls the loyalty service, so the storefront reads core fields and the new field in one query. Points out that resolver fetch is restricted to the Project host allowlist, so the loyalty host must be added. Describes the CLI flow (init, pnpm test, pnpm dev against the deployed CIL, pnpm validate, pnpm push waiting for the revision to be running).
expectations: Recommends a schema extension (typeDefs and resolvers on the extension subgraph), not a Managed API Extension
Adds the field to the Product entity so it composes with core Product fields in one query
Mentions adding the loyalty service host to the Project allowlist for resolver fetch
Describes testing the composed schema locally with pnpm dev before pushing
Treats the push as done only when the new revision reports running

evals.prompt: I ran pnpm push for our CIL extension bundle and CI went green with --no-wait, but the new field doesn't show up in the Experience API. extension status shows the new version. What's going on?
evals.expected_output: Explains that a push stores the bundle and the runtime loads it afterwards, moving the revision from pending to running or failed. extension status shows the stored bundle, not whether it loaded. With --no-wait the load verdict was never checked; a failed revision drops out of service and the Project keeps serving the newest revision that did not fail. Recommends pushing with the wait (raising --wait-timeout if needed), checking the live schema with explore --deployed, and running validate locally to catch sandbox violations such as process or node: imports.
expectations: Explains that extension status shows the stored bundle, not whether the revision loaded
Identifies that the revision probably failed to load and the Project keeps serving the newest revision that did not fail
Recommends pushing with the wait on (raising --wait-timeout) instead of --no-wait
Recommends checking the live composed schema with explore --deployed

evals.prompt: After an order is placed through our CIL storefront, we need to send it to our ERP. Should I write a Managed API Extension on order create for that?
evals.expected_output: Routes away from a Managed API Extension: the ERP call happens after the write is persisted, so it belongs in a commercetools Subscription outside the bundle (for example a Connect event app), not in the synchronous write path where a slow or failing ERP call would block order creation.
expectations: Recommends a commercetools Subscription (or a Connect event app triggered by one) instead of a Managed API Extension
Explains that work after a write is persisted belongs outside the extension bundle
Notes that a synchronous ERP call in the write path would slow or block order creation
